brief: The allotment block — 21 plots, the longest untouched part of the town — already grows vegetables: SPECIES carries carrots, cabbages, beans and pumpkins flagged veg:1, and speciesFor() splits the CA on inAllotment(). What it has is half a cycle. A mature carrot sits at bSt 3 until the same age-and-crowding dieback that clears a rose removes it at random. Nothing is ever picked. Add harvest as a real term: a mature veg cell can be taken, by the `allot` gardener who already walks in through the gate, kneels at a real BED cell and leaves (spawn at ~line 935, kneel at ~792), and a cleared row then re-seeds. The observable outcome is that the allotments visibly turn over — rows fill, get cleared and come back — instead of drifting to a static full block.
successLooksLike: Watched over several days the allotment rows fill, empty and refill, and a gardener who kneels leaves with something rather than only putting something in.
avoid: Do not add a fifth vegetable — four exist and the census counts them. Do not give the flower ring a harvest; dieback there is correct and the ring is meant to be decorative.
